description:
## What

When DNS resolution or DNSSEC validation fails during verify_tls_server's DANE attempt, what happens?

## Options

- **A) Opportunistic.** DNS / DNSSEC failure -> use PKIX result. Behaves like a soft suggestion. Active attacker blocking DNS can downgrade to PKIX-only. Matches RFC 7672 SMTP-DANE deployment reality. Best for adoption (won't break consumers in flaky-network environments).

- **B) Strict-DANE.** DNS / DNSSEC failure = verification failure. Refuses to fall back. Stronger security; brittle in flaky-network environments. Matches strict-security stances.

- **C) Operator-configurable, default opportunistic.** Both modes available; default opportunistic for adoption-friendliness. Strict-security deployments opt into strict mode via runtime config. Adds one knob.

## Considerations

- HTTPS-DANE has no standardized failure-mode answer.
- SMTP-DANE (RFC 7672) specifies opportunistic.
- 'Encourage DANE to spread without consumer code change' goal aligns with opportunistic default (won't break working PKIX validations).
- Strict mode is occasionally requested by regulated / high-assurance consumers.

## Deferred

Mark 2026-05-12: deferred. Needs answer before PKIX-j32w.3 (pkix-chain integration) lands.

## Decision-gate

Human-labeled. Surface when implementation work on .3 starts.
title: Decide DANE failure mode (opportunistic vs strict-DANE vs operator-configurable)
